title: Learning Salah (Getting Started)
summary: What Salah is, the five daily prayers, and where to find the full step-by-step guide.

body.text: A starting point for practice, not a replacement for learning in person

Salah is the ritual prayer performed five times a day, made up of a set sequence of standing, bowing, and prostrating, paired with short Arabic recitations. It's enough to start practising by following an illustrated guide — but reading it is not a substitute for having someone show you in person at least once, ideally at a mosque, since small physical details (exact hand position, pacing) come across far better shown than described. Don't worry about performing it perfectly from day one; that comes with practice.

body.caption: Sujud — prostration is one of the core positions of every rak'ah

body.text: Fajr (dawn, before sunrise), Dhuhr (midday), Asr (mid-afternoon), Maghrib (just after sunset), and Isha (night). Each one has a valid time window, shown on this app's Home dashboard and Prayer tab based on your location. Each prayer consists of a set number of units called rak'ahs, ranging from two rak'ahs (Fajr) to four (Dhuhr, Asr, Isha), with Maghrib at three.

body.translation: And seek help through patience and prayer.

body.question: Do I need to know Arabic before I can start praying?
body.answer: The recitations within Salah are in Arabic, but you're not expected to already know them — you learn this small, fixed set of short, frequently repeated phrases gradually. Transliteration and translation are available throughout this app's Quran and Dua sections precisely so you can start learning them at your own pace rather than waiting until you feel "ready."

body.question: Head to the Prayer tab for the full rak'ah-by-rak'ah walkthrough. Reading through it once before you first try to pray can make the actual attempt much less daunting.
